headline: Histology and spatial omics are mapping single-cell states in 2D and 3D tissue
label: Single Cell Spatial Omics Inference
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair H&E morphology and spatial omics to infer single-cell molecular states and 3D tissue architecture.
synthesis: The common thread is computational recovery of single-cell molecular and spatial information from histology images and spatial omics data. SCOPE predicts single-cell RNA and protein levels from H&E, and VirTues-M2 jointly learns H&E morphology and spatial proteomics for tissue-level analysis. REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence to inferred spatial gene expression, and Dancer separates within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. Other items address the 3D axis: Space-map aligns serial sections into single-cell atlases, GenVinci reconstructs 3D tissue from histology to map senescence, and a rotation-equivariant network reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds. CIRCA adds identifiable cell and niche programs. What is new is single-cell resolution combined with 3D and multimodal inference from routine stains, with reliability and identifiability increasingly addressed.
